Configure the CrowdStrike Falcon sensor on iPhone and iPad — which tenant and cloud the device registers with, and how the host is identified once it appears in the Falcon console.
On iOS these values are not delivered as a standalone app configuration: they go in the VendorConfig dictionary of a Content Filter payload whose filter identifier is com.crowdstrike.falconmobile. Build the dictionary here, then paste it into that payload’s custom data.
The human-readable description of this payload. This description appears on the Detail screen.
The human-readable name for the profile payload. The name appears on the Detail screen and doesn’t need to be unique.

The reverse-DNS-style identifier for the payload. This identifier is usually the same as the TopLevel value, with an additional appended component. This string must be unique within the profile. During a profile replacement, the system updates payloads with the same ‘PayloadIdentifier’ and ‘PayloadUUID’ in the old and new profiles.
The payload type, which each payload domain’s reference page specifies.

The globally unique identifier for the payload. The actual content is unimportant, but must be globally unique. In macOS, use ‘uuidgen’ to generate UUIDs. During a profile replacement, the system updates payloads with the same ‘PayloadIdentifier’ and ‘PayloadUUID’ in the old and new profiles.
The version of this specific payload.
The human-readable string containing the name of the organization that provides the profile. This value doesn’t need to match the organization payload value in the enclosing dictionary.

Your CrowdStrike customer ID checksum (CCID).
Find it in the Falcon console under Host setup and management › Deploy › Sensor downloads.

The Falcon cloud your tenant lives in — us-1, us-2, eu-1, us-gov-1, and so on.
Take the value from the MDM enrolment wizard in the Falcon console rather than typing it by hand.
Provisioning token that authorises the sensor to register with your tenant.
This value is a credential. Deliver it in an encrypted profile, never in a plain-text profile committed to source control, and rotate it if it is ever exported in the clear.
Falcon API host the sensor reports to, as given by the MDM enrolment wizard for your cloud.

Email address of the device’s assigned user, used to identify the host in the Falcon console.
Use your MDM’s user variable so it is filled in per device — $EMAIL in Jamf Pro, {{mail}} in Intune.
The MDM’s own identifier for this device, carried into the Falcon host record so the two inventories can be reconciled.

Grouping tags applied to the host at registration, so it lands in the right host groups without a manual step.
List them comma-separated, with no spaces.

Whether the sensor skips the legal notice the user would otherwise have to accept on first launch.
Set this only where your organisation has told users separately what the sensor collects.
